title: Boundary Handling
text: Standard LOESS neighbourhoods become asymmetric boundaries: fewer points exist one side, pulling local fit toward data interior. boundary_policy parameter controls data padded mitigate effect.

title: Boundary Handling
text: Pads beyond endpoints replicating first last observed values. Prevents fit curling toward zero safe default nearly use cases. Use : strong prior boundary behaviour; general-purpose smoothing.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(boundary_policy = "extend") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (extend policy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (extend policy): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4897657 0.4961584 0.5029665 0.5102219 0.5179564 0.5262019

title: Boundary Handling
text: Mirrors data endpoints fitting, discards reflected region output. Preserves continuity derivatives endpoints. Use : Circular data (e.g., angle, day--year), symmetric physical quantities, derivative boundary expected zero.

title: LOESS Concepts
text: LOESS (Locally Estimated Scatterplot Smoothing) nonparametric regression method fits smooth curves scatter plots without assuming global functional form. Unlike parametric methods (linear regression, polynomial fitting), LOESS adapts locally data structure, making ideal : Exploratory data analysis — Discover patterns without assumptions Trend estimation — Extract signals noisy time series Baseline correction — Remove systematic effects spectroscopy Genomic smoothing — Smooth methylation, ChIP-seq, expression data

title: LOESS Concepts
text: point data, LOESS: Selects neighbors — Choose nearest points (controlled fraction) Assigns weights — Closer points get higher weights (using kernel function) Fits locally — Perform weighted least squares regression Extracts value — Use fitted value smoothed estimate Iterates (optional) — Reweight points based residuals reduce outlier influence

title: LOESS Concepts
text: fraction (also called bandwidth span) important parameter. controls proportion data used local fit. Tip: Start fraction=0.67 (default) adjust based visual inspection. Use cross-validation automated selection.

title: Custom Weights
text: Per-observation weights encode data quality directly LOESS fit. effective weight observation jj local fit centred xix_i : wij=custom_weights[j]×K(dijhi)×rjw_{ij} = \text{custom\_weights}[j] \times K\!\left(\frac{d_{ij}}{h_i}\right) \times r_j Note: custom_weights applies Batch mode .

title: Custom Weights
code: library(rfastloess)  x <- 1:10 y <- x * 2.0 y[6] <- 100.0              # spike at index 6  weights <- rep(1.0, 10) weights[6] <- 0.0          # exclude the spike  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5, iterations = 0L) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights) cat("First 6 smoothed values (outlier excluded, no robustness):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (outlier excluded, no robustness): print(head(result$y)) #> [1]  2.572621  4.000000  6.000000  8.000000 10.000000 12.000000

code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.5)  sigma <- 0.1 + 0.5 * abs(sin(x)) weights <- 1 / sigma^2  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.3) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights)  plot(x, y, pch = 16, cex = 0.5 + weights / max(weights),     col = "gray", main = "Inverse-Variance Weighted LOESS") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

title: Polynomial Degree
text: target point, LOESS fits polynomial neighbouring data using weighted least squares. degree parameter controls order polynomial. Degree can specified integer (0L–4L) string ("constant", "linear", "quadratic", "cubic", "quartic").

title: Polynomial Degree
text: fit point weighted mean. Produces smooth results ignores local slope, introducing bias wherever true function changes. Use : Maximum smoothness matters accuracy; computationally cheapest.

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Fits weighted line neighbourhood. Removes first-order bias handles boundary regions correctly. right choice vast majority applications. Use : Default; monotone gently curved data; boundary accuracy matters.
code: model <- Loess(degree = "linear", fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (linear local regression):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (linear local regression): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4758389 0.4846388 0.4944609 0.5054102 0.5169758 0.5286606

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Fits weighted parabola. Captures curvature data reduces bias regions strong local curvature, cost higher variance. Use : Data visible curvature local extrema; use larger fraction stabilise fit.
code: model <- Loess(degree = "quadratic", fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (quadratic local regression):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (quadratic local regression): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4043043 0.4131994 0.4244604 0.4384709 0.4565813 0.4791656

title: Polynomial Degree
text: Cubic quartic local fits capture inflections fine structure require sufficiently large neighbourhood remain stable. Rarely needed practice. Use : Highly non-linear local structure; combine larger fraction.
code: model <- Loess(degree = "cubic", fraction = 0.6) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (cubic local regression):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (cubic local regression): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4183075 0.4299695 0.4442197 0.4608883 0.4798054 0.5008015

title: Polynomial Degree
text: dataset boundary, neighbourhood one-sided may contain enough points support requested degree. Setting boundary_degree_fallback = TRUE automatically reduces degree boundaries avoid instability.

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Standard LOESS operates single predictor x. LOESS extends n-dimensional predictor space passing matrix x, enabling surface smoothing spatial grids, time–altitude combinations, similar multi-predictor datasets. Note: Neighbourhood search scales number dimensions. d ≥ 3 keep fraction small consider "interpolation" surface mode (default) reduce computation.

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Single predictor. configuration required.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 200) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(200, sd = 0.2)  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.3) result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (1D LOESS):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (1D LOESS): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.3808654 0.3912167 0.4028709 0.4154835 0.4286045 0.4422857

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Two predictors (e.g., latitude/longitude, time/altitude). Pass n × 2 matrix x.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 100 lat <- runif(n, -pi, pi) lon <- runif(n, -pi, pi) z   <- sin(lat) + cos(lon) + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)  x2d <- cbind(lat, lon)   # n × 2 matrix  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.3, dimensions = 2L) result <- fit(model, x2d, z) cat("First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, lat/lon):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, lat/lon): print(head(result$y)) #> [1]  0.17983519  0.02191686 -0.01849028  0.22186652  0.09969107 -0.22507546

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: Pass n × d matrix x. Higher dimensions require larger fraction keep local neighbourhood populated.
code: set.seed(42) n <- 200 x1 <- runif(n) x2 <- runif(n) x3 <- runif(n) y  <- x1 + sin(2 * pi * x2) + x3^2 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1)  x3d <- cbind(x1, x2, x3)   # n × 3 matrix  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.5, dimensions = 3L) result <- fit(model, x3d, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (3D LOESS):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (3D LOESS): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.8070023 0.9764349 0.8780069 1.0434288 0.9838051 0.8222218

title: Multivariate LOESS
text: multivariate mode, neighbour distances can computed different metrics.
code: # Reuse the 2D spatial data from above; upweight the lat dimension model <- Loess(     fraction = 0.3,     dimensions = 2L,     distance_metric = "weighted",     weighted_metric_weights = c(2.0, 1.0)  # lat counts twice ) result <- fit(model, x2d, z) cat("First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, weighted distance):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (2D LOESS, weighted distance): print(head(result$y)) #> [1]  0.17709387  0.08359416 -0.05142187  0.14223791  0.12033868 -0.13208634

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Kernel functions determine neighbouring points contribute local fit. Points closer target receive higher weights.

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Efficiency = AMISE relative Epanechnikov (1.0 = optimal)

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Cleveland’s original choice. Best -around performance. w(u)=(1−|u|3)3w(u) = (1 - |u|^3)^3 Use : Default choice applications.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(weight_function = "tricube") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (tricube kernel):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (tricube kernel): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4897657 0.4961584 0.5029665 0.5102219 0.5179564 0.5262019

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Optimal AMISE sense. Slightly angular tricube. w(u)=34(1−u2)w(u) = \frac{3}{4}(1 - u^2) Use : Statistical optimality matters; compact support desired.

title: Merge Strategies
text: Streaming LOESS processes data fixed-size chunks configurable overlap. Points inside overlap zone receive estimates adjacent chunks; merge strategy decides two estimates reconciled.

title: Merge Strategies
text: Assigns overlap point weight proportional proximity centre respective chunk: points near left-chunk centre favour left estimate; points near right-chunk centre favour right. Minimises boundary artefacts. Use : Minimising boundary artefacts important speed; moderate overlap (10–20% chunk size) used.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3) x_chunk <- x[seq_len(50)] y_chunk <- y[seq_len(50)]  model <- StreamingLoess(     merge_strategy = "weighted_average",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (weighted_average strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (weighted_average strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Takes arithmetic mean left-chunk right-chunk estimates overlap region. Fast sufficient chunks similar smoothing quality. Use : Chunks large overlap region uniform data density.
code: model <- StreamingLoess(     merge_strategy = "average",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (average strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (average strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Keeps left-chunk estimate overlap zone discards right-chunk estimate. Produces left-flush output. Use : need final output values immediately chunk (look-ahead revision); left-chunk context dominates.

title: Robustness
text: Standard LOESS can biased outliers. Robustness iterations downweight points large residuals: Fit initial LOESS Compute residuals Assign robustness weights (large residuals → low weight) Refit using combined distance × robustness weights Repeat steps 2–4

title: Robustness
text: w(u)={(1−u2)2|u|<10|u|≥1w(u) = \begin{cases} (1 - u^2)^2 & |u| < 1 \\ 0 & |u| \geq 1 \end{cases} Use : General purpose, balanced approach.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "bisquare") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (bisquare robustness):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (bisquare robustness): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4897657 0.4961584 0.5029665 0.5102219 0.5179564 0.5262019

title: Robustness
text: Linear penalty beyond threshold. Less aggressive Bisquare. w(u)={1|u|≤kk/|u||u|>kw(u) = \begin{cases} 1 & |u| \leq k \\ k/|u| & |u| > k \end{cases} Use : Moderate outliers, want retain influence.
code: model <- Loess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "huber") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (huber robustness):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (huber robustness): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4999039 0.5072430 0.5150605 0.5233922 0.5322738 0.5417411

title: Robustness
text: Hard threshold — points threshold excluded completely. w(u)={1|u|≤k0|u|>kw(u) = \begin{cases} 1 & |u| \leq k \\ 0 & |u| > k \end{cases} Use : Extreme outliers, want binary exclusion.
code: model <- Loess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "talwar") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (talwar robustness):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (talwar robustness): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4730281 0.4784755 0.4842521 0.4903763 0.4968663 0.5037406

title: Scaling Methods
text: iterations > 0, LOESS computes robustness weights comparing residual current residual scale estimate σ̂\hat{\sigma}. scaling_method parameter controls σ̂\hat{\sigma} estimated. wi=B(|ri|6⋅σ̂)w_i = B\!\left(\frac{|r_i|}{6 \cdot \hat{\sigma}}\right)

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri−median(ri)|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i - \text{median}(r_i)|) First centers residuals median, takes median absolute deviations. Double use median makes highly resistant extreme outliers. Use : Data may contain outliers (default applications).
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Loess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mad") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (MAD scaling):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (MAD scaling): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.4897657 0.4961584 0.5029665 0.5102219 0.5179564 0.5262019

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i|) Uses uncentered median — unlike MAD subtract residual median first. Still robust (median-based), faster (one partial sort instead two). Use : Speed matters data minimal systematic bias residuals.
code: model <- Loess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mar") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("First 6 smoothed values (MAR scaling):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (MAR scaling): print(head(result$y)) #> [1] 0.5096452 0.5176529 0.5262527 0.5354995 0.5454482 0.5561534

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=1n∑|ri|\hat{\sigma} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |r_i| Arithmetic mean absolute residuals. Non-robust: single extreme outlier inflates σ̂\hat{\sigma}, causing bisquare weight function -downweight outliers. Use : Clean data outliers; maximum computation speed required.

title: Use Case: Genomic Data Smoothing
text: small fraction = 0.1 lets LOESS follow fine-scale spatial structure without smearing transitions methylated unmethylated regions. confidence_intervals = 0.95 produces uncertainty bands naturally widen positions sparser CpG coverage, making low-confidence segments immediately apparent plot.
code: library(rfastloess)  set.seed(42) n <- 1000 positions <- sort(runif(n, 0, 1e6))  true_meth <- 0.5 + 0.3 * sin(positions / 1e5) observed  <- true_meth + rnorm(n, sd = 0.15) observed  <- pmax(0, pmin(1, observed))  model <- Loess(     fraction = 0.1,     iterations = 3,     confidence_intervals = 0.95 ) result <- fit(model, positions, observed)  plot(positions, observed, pch = ".", col = "gray",     xlab = "Genomic Position (bp)", ylab = "Methylation Level",     main = "Methylation Profile Smoothing") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_lower, col = "blue", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_upper, col = "blue", lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Observed", "Smoothed", "95% CI"),         pch = c(1, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, 2),         col = c("gray", "blue", "blue"))

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: window_capacity = 25 limits internal buffer 25 recent observations; add_point call costs O(window) rather growing total history. min_points = 5 suppresses output window holds enough points stable fit — calls made threshold return NULL. update_mode = "incremental" re-fits recent point rather full window, halving typical latency modest accuracy cost.

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
code: library(rfastloess)  set.seed(42) times        <- 1:100 temperatures <- 20 + 5 * sin(times / 10) + rnorm(100)  model <- OnlineLoess(     fraction = 0.3,     window_capacity = 25,     min_points = 5,     update_mode = "incremental" ) for (i in seq_along(times)) {     result <- add_point(model, times[i], temperatures[i])     if (!is.null(result))         cat(sprintf("Time %d: %.2f\n", times[i], result$y))     if (i >= 10) break  # print only the first few outputs } #> Time 5: 22.80 #> Time 6: 22.72 #> Time 7: 24.73 #> Time 8: 23.49 #> Time 9: 25.94 #> Time 10: 24.14

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: fraction = 0.1 sizes neighbourhood 10% data evaluation point — narrow enough follow slowly varying trend without smearing periodic variation. Three robustness iterations -weight noise spikes bias fitted curve; especially important signal--noise ratio low occasional outliers expected.
code: library(rfastloess)  set.seed(42) t <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 500) trend <- 10 + 0.5 * t + 3 * sin(t / 10) noise <- rnorm(500, sd = 3) y <- trend + noise  model <- Loess(fraction = 0.1, iterations = 3) result <- fit(model, t, y)  plot(t, y, col = "gray", pch = ".",     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Value", main = "Trend Extraction") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("Observed", "Trend (LOESS)"),         pch = c(1, NA), lty = c(NA, 1), col = c("gray", "blue"))

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Setting return_residuals = TRUE stores observed − smoothed alongside smooth. slightly wider fraction = 0.4 produces smoother baseline trend, short-duration oscillations end residuals rather absorbed trend component. residual series ready spectral analysis, seasonality detection, change-point methods.
code: library(rfastloess) set.seed(42)  t        <- 1:120 trend    <- 100 + 0.5 * t seasonal <- 15 * sin(2 * pi * t / 12) noise    <- rnorm(120, sd = 5) y        <- trend + seasonal + noise  model    <- Loess(fraction = 0.4, iterations = 2) result   <- fit(model, t, y) residual <- y - result$y  par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 0.5)) plot(t, y, type = "l", col = "gray",     main = "Original + LOESS Trend", xlab = "Month", ylab = "Value") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)  plot(t, residual, type = "l", col = "darkgreen",     main = "Detrended Residual (Seasonal Component)",     xlab = "Month", ylab = "Residual") abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "red") par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

text: implementation robust R’s loess due two key design choices: MAD-Based Scale Estimation: robustness weight calculations, crate uses Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) scale estimation: contrast, R’s loess uses median absolute residuals (MAR): MAD breakdown-point-optimal estimator—remains valid even 50% data outliers. median-centering step removes asymmetric bias residual distributions. MAD provides consistent outlier detection regardless whether residuals centered around zero. Boundary Padding: crate applies range different boundary policies dataset edges: Extend: Repeats edge values maintain local neighborhood size. Reflect: Mirrors data symmetrically around boundaries. Zero: Pads zeros (useful signal processing). NoBoundary: Original Cleveland behavior R’s loess apply boundary padding, can lead : Biased estimates near boundaries due asymmetric local neighborhoods. Default: 3. weight_function Kernel weight function. One "tricube" (default), "gaussian", "uniform" (alias: "boxcar"), "cosine", "epanechnikov", "biweight" (alias: "bisquare"), "triangle" (alias: "triangular"). robustness_method Outlier downweighting method: "bisquare" (default; alias: "biweight"), "huber", "talwar". scaling_method Residual scale estimation robustness weights: "mad" (default; alias: "median_absolute_deviation"), "mar" (alias: "median_absolute_residual"), "mean" (alias: "mean_absolute_residual"). boundary_policy Boundary handling strategy: "extend" (default; alias: "pad"), "reflect" (alias: "mirror"), "zero", "noboundary" (alias: "none"). zero_weight_fallback Fallback policy robustness weights drop zero: "use_local_mean" (default; aliases: "local_mean", "mean"), "return_original" (alias: "original"), "return_none" (alias: "none"). auto_converge Convergence tolerance early stopping robustness iterations. NULL (default) disables early stopping. return_diagnostics Logical; TRUE, return fit-quality metrics (RMSE, MAE, R-squared, AIC, etc.). Default: FALSE. return_residuals Logical; TRUE, return residuals result. Default: FALSE. return_robustness_weights Logical; TRUE, return per-point robustness weights. Default: FALSE. merge_strategy Strategy reconciling overlapping chunk regions: "weighted_average" (default; alias: "weighted"), "average" (alias: "mean"), "take_first" (alias: "first"), "take_last" (alias: "last"). parallel Logical; enable parallel processing. Default: TRUE. degree Local polynomial degree: "constant", "linear" (default), "quadratic", "cubic", "quartic". dimensions Number predictor dimensions. Default: 1. distance_metric Distance metric neighbourhood computation: "normalized" (default), "euclidean", "manhattan", "chebyshev", "minkowski", "weighted". Use "minkowski:p" set custom p value. surface_mode Surface evaluation mode: "interpolation" (default) "direct". return_se Logical; TRUE, compute hat-matrix statistics (effective degrees freedom, leverage, standard errors). Default: FALSE. confidence_intervals Confidence level confidence intervals (e.g., 0.95). NULL (default) disables confidence intervals. prediction_intervals Confidence level prediction intervals (e.g., 0.95). NULL (default) disables prediction intervals. weighted_metric_weights Numeric vector per-dimension weights used distance_metric = "weighted". Length must equal dimensions. NULL (default) uses equal weights. cell Cell size tuning parameter interpolation grid. NULL (default) uses library default. interpolation_vertices Number vertices interpolation grid. NULL (default) uses library default. boundary_degree_fallback Logical; TRUE, fall back lower polynomial degree boundaries fitting requested degree fails. NULL (default) uses library default.
